text: Write the four kinds of method reference. Fill in the four blanks.
choices: Consumer<String> a = ___;           // a method on a particular object
Function<String,Integer> c = ___;   // an instance method, receiver as argument
explanation: Verified: `hi`, then `7 5 []`. The third is the one that confuses people — `String::length` looks static and is not; the receiver becomes the first argument, which is what makes `Person::name` usable as a `Function<Person,String>` in a stream. Java works this out from the target type, which is convenient and occasionally produces an error message that takes some reading.
